The Tribunal is not very much interested in whether it was the -- on who had the primacy between the SDS and the SDA for the preservation of the former state of Yugoslavia. It disintegrated in any case. So let's go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I ask just one more in this area, please? Just one more?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Trbojevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You will remember that before the war operation started, in the assembly of Bosnia and Herzegovina, political activity started for the constitutional guarantees and procedures to be established so that the vital interests of all the peoples in Bosnia-Herzegovina should be secured in a certain sense. Those activities had started, hadn't they?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, they had, but the disintegration took place before we managed to assert them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't hear your sentence.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, the disintegration occurred before those guarantees were embodied in the constitution. That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So now we come to the war operations in Croatia. Would you agree with me that both the constitutional and legal role of the JNA was to preserve the territorial integrity and sovereignty of SFRY according to the constitution and laws that were still in force at the time?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I would agree with you, and if possible, could I have the text of the translation on my screen? Because in that way, I can tell when the translation has been completed and when I can start speaking so there is no overlapping. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the political position of the SDA, which gave instructions not to take part in the war operations in Croatia at the time, was not in conformity with the constitution, was it?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC
utterances.text: I would only partially agree with you in that respect. And I've already confirmed this in my previous answer, and that is that the Yugoslav People's Army was one of the mechanisms whereby the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia was to have been preserved. However, in the constitution of the former Yugoslavia, it was -- the implication was it was an enemy and an aggression, I don't think the constitution of any country envisages that the army of that country should attack its own people, because the Yugoslav People's Army, by its definition, was an army of all the peoples of Yugoslavia. Therefore, of the Slovenes and Croats as well, as in those days. Unfortunately, the Yugoslav People's Army was directly attacking civilians and civilian property as well, and destroying civilian facilities in Croatia, that is something that we didn't want to take part in, and I think that that was quite justified and in harmony with the constitution.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you say that the military response of Croatia after it was internationally recognised, and after the JNA did not wish to leave that territory, was justified?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC
utterances.text: That is a complex issue that I could not give a simple answer to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In any event, no one expects us to resolve all political disputes here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise, Your Honour, for this remark.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said, on the 27th of May this year, that constitutional activity after the first multi-party election started with the dispute over the oaths, and you elaborated on this with the request of the SDS that remaining in Yugoslavia should be given a first place in that text. Could you recollect any other detail in this context? If I tell you that the administrative service distributed to the deputies the text which was any way a constitutional provision, which was already part of the constitution, and then somebody observed that the text was not identical, and then there was a break during which the Presidents of the deputy clubs got together, Mr. Izetbegovic, Karadzic, and other party leaders who were not deputies, and then a new text of the oath was agreed among the parties, was that how it went?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC
utterances.text: To the best of my recollection, the text of the oath that was distributed to us first was the authentic text which the deputies spoke out when taking their oath for years. So to the best of my recollection, we received the same wording used by all Members of Parliament before. It wasn't changed. But as the order of the words in the oath was that the first one should take an oath of allegiance to Bosnia-Herzegovina and then to Yugoslavia, the SDS complained, and that is when the problem arose. They wanted a change in the oath of allegiance before the deputies had taken the oath. And this was impossible. It couldn't be done before the deputies took their oath because, before that, they weren't really Members of Parliament.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But it was agreed and changed, because the sociopolitical situation had changed and words -- socialism, was left out?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Trbojevic, what's the relevance of this event?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we are talking about the confrontation of different policies. Mr. Mujadzic has expressed that from the very outset, in the assembly, there was a confrontation, because of the request that he described. I'm trying to -- we have finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Let's proceed, move forward, because we are not going to waste time on the debate that took place in the assembly on the formulation of the oath, on how it should have been drafted or whether it should have included this and what should have come first. Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll move on to the events in Prijedor. In the LiveNote, in the Stakic case, page 3.649, and in other places too, you spoke about the Territorial Defence not having weapons so that the assessment was that Prijedor could not be defended. And at one point, you said that the Muslim people wouldn't have anything to defend themselves with if it were to be attacked by the JNA or the SDS. Did you mean that the SDS could have, on its own, carried out that attack?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let him answer the question and then I will hear your objection, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, just a moment please for me to think this over.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. While you think, when I stopped you, Mr. Koumjian, provided that what has been suggested by Mr. Trbojevic to the witness is not correct, in other words, that he did not mention a possible attack from the SDS? If the suggestion is correct, then wait until we hear the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: The question included an unintentional oversimplification of the witness's testimony. He never said the Territorial Defence had no weapons. He described the paucity, the poorness of the weapons of the Territorial Defence but the question implies that he I think unintentionally that he said that he had no weapons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Dr. Mujadzic, please do take that in consideration.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't mean it in absolute terms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Mr. Trbojevic, as well. Yes, Mr. Mujadzic, please. Do you require more time to answer the question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I can answer it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The observation that the Territorial Defence didn't have any weapons, you have already heard from Mr. Koumjian. The Territorial Defence did have some weapons, after all, and that was light infantry weapons, and these were mostly hunting rifles or personal weapons that people had lawfully. There were about 1.000 barrels that Colonel Arsic distributed legally to mobilise the Territorial Defence, and some weapons were procured by people on their own, on the black market, and in fact, those weapons were mostly purchased from Serbs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Wait. I'm going to stop you, because the substance of Mr. Trbojevic's question wasn't actually what extent of ammunition or -- and weapons did the Territorial Defence have, but whether, in including or in referring to a possible attack on -- the possibility of defending themselves against possible attacks, you had also included a possible attack from the SDS, whether you sincerely believe that the SDS was in a position to attack the Muslims in your region. Not the JNA, not the JNA, because he said JNA and SDS. Forget the JNA for the time being. Was there the perception that the SDS could launch an attack on its own?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the question put by Mr. Trbojevic was put in such a way that I am asked to say whether the SDS could have attacked Bosniaks without the JNA, and the gist of it all is that many months before there was any possibility of an attack, what was happening within the JNA itself, which underwent dynamic changes in its composition and its officer structure, identified itself fully with the policies of Mr. Milosevic and the SDS. Therefore, the question of the JNA is inseparable from the SDS. The JNA was transformed into the military wing of the SDS. So the -- Milosevic's policies served as the political background for the JNA.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Trbojevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've explained about the part of the weapons given to the Territorial Defence, the reserve police, private hunting weapons, and if we remember the telegram from Mr. Halilovic that we looked at today, I think there is no need to show it to the witness again. What weapons is Mr. Halilovic referring to when he says -- when he makes his allegations about you? Which weapons was he referring to?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Halilovic had information about the arming of the Territorial Defence, and the overall weaponry in the possession of Bosniaks, and that is what he was referring to probably.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us remind ourselves of the other telegram of the 29th of April, 1992, that was shown to you in the police and in the barracks -- by the police and in the barracks, signed by Mr. Delimustafic, and which includes an order to build a road barrier, not to allow equipment and materiel to be taken out of the barracks, et cetera, et cetera. You said that that must be a non-authentic document, and you highlighted certain things that were illogical in that text. Would you agree with me that the scenario of blocking barracks and not allowing the troops to leave, to come out, and take out the weapons and materiel, was a scenario that had already been seen in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Such things did indeed happen in Slovenia and Croatia, but there was an enormous difference between the situation in Slovenia, that of Croatia, and the one in Bosnia and Herzegovina. If you remember, Slovenia kept all the weapons of the Territorial Defence, because it did not allow the TO weapons to be taken away so that it even had heavy artillery weapons, anti-armour weapons, and thereby was in a position to resist and oppose the JNA. The Croatia didn't succeed in doing so but it had wide open borders with Italy and Hungary and it also had a chance of arming itself and resisting the army in that way. Bosnia and Herzegovina had no possibility of arming itself, and it didn't have such weapons, and these activities in Bosnia and Herzegovina could simply have not been carried out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Supposing that this could have been a forgery and that it was provocative in nature and called for a response, that is what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC
utterances.text: Is that your question?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, that was the case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this context, the event which took place on the 30th of April and the 1st of May, could it be a reaction, a response, to this dispatch?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, do you mean -- was it possible for the Bosniak side to react to this dispatch?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, the Serb side.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC
utterances.text: I see. If Serbs believed that it was true and authentic, would their reaction -- I'm sorry, I don't fully understand your question. It's not precise enough.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that it could have been expected that this -- this dispatch could have been expected to be unauthentic, untrue, designed to provoke a reaction. Is that what you had in mind?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In connection with the events of the 30th of April, you said that there were soldiers around the town, that certain citizens recognise members of both Prijedor brigades, that there were special police units from other towns as well, and that this indicated that the action had been planned at the regional level. Can you explain what exactly you had in mind?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC
utterances.text: Since citizens of Prijedor who had lived together for years know each other very well, Bosniak and Croat citizens were able to recognise amongst the soldiers who, after the event, appeared in Prijedor, there were a lot of those who were not originally from the area of Prijedor. Some people even recognised individuals coming from the area of Sanski Most, for instance, and other locations. So it was obvious that not only Prijedor units took part in this action but also units from some other towns, which is what I based my testimony on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. We'll have a break now. 15 minutes. How much longer do you reckon you have, Mr. Trbojevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 15 minutes or so, 20 perhaps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you have 15 minutes, just feel free to tell me yes or no, may I suggest to the interpreters and the technicians that we go ahead and then we can finish and all go home?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes? I can't see much behind the -- okay. So let's go -- let's go ahead. And if the technicians need a stop, an interval to change the tape, please let us know. Thank you. Yes, Mr. Trbojevic, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You continue, then, to say that some later information pointed to an even higher level of planning of this action. You said a much higher level. What did you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC
utterances.text: Immediately after this event, there appeared a number of blue posters all over Prijedor town with the following words: Citizens of Prijedor, Muslims, there is no need to worry. The security situation in Prijedor is now stable. I'm paraphrasing the text. I'm not using the authentic words. However, the essence of the text on those posters was the following: We merely wish to remove the representatives of the party for democratic action who had destroyed the economy of Prijedor, who had plundered Prijedor, and who had -- who are responsible for the chaotic situation in Prijedor. In this way, we are trying to save you from them, and after six months, you will have -- you will enjoy the full right to elect, at a new election, your new genuine representatives, and not these thieves, these criminals, who have brought this down into such a difficult situation. This political text, which I have now simplified and paraphrased, was much more eloquent and precise. It had been composed in very precise and eloquent terms, and obviously it had been prepared long time ago, because these posters appeared around the town the very next morning. So it was necessary to compose the text, to have it printed, and this is -- this could not have been done within one hour or one night. This just tells you that the whole thing had been planned a long time ago. Then the media continued, or rather started with their propaganda, using very similar texts, and Bosniaks were then asked to return their weapons and the whole problem focused for a while on the SDA, that is the extremist wing of the SDA. Knowing what the positions were of the local leadership, and also knowing who they were, knowing the local SDS leaders, how skillful politically they were, this perfectly coordinated military and political action could not have come from the local level, the municipal level, of the SDS leadership, but only from a higher level. At the very least, there were certain instructions. I'm not saying that the whole plan, the whole action, was masterminded at the high level, but I'm sure that certain instructions and guidelines were given from the highest level. For instance, when it comes to the wording of this text and some other details.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. In a previous testimony, in the Stakic case, page 3.677, when speaking of the Prijedor municipal Crisis Staff, you stated that this was an institution that was above all other institutions. Do you want me to show you the decision on the establishment of the Prijedor municipal Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC
utterances.text: Are you referring to the Crisis Staff of the Serbian Municipality of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am referring to the Crisis Staff in the Prijedor municipality which functioned after the 30th of April.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC
utterances.text: Please, just emphasise that you are referring to the Crisis Staff the Serbian Municipality of Prijedor, because I understood you to mean that you were referring to a -- to this body, specific body in general.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We have a technical problem. I think we are having a -- we are hearing simultaneously with the translation, the original, over a loudspeaker inside the courtroom. Okay. Can we go ahead?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's not the case with my earphones, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It was in my case, any way. Okay. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown Exhibit P1265? It was exhibited in the Stakic case under number 110, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The date in question is the 20th of May, in Article 2 we see that the Crisis Staff of Prijedor is established in order to coordinate government and so on and so forth. What interests me in this case is Article 3. I should like to draw your attention to the following: "The Crisis Staff shall decide on issues within the competence of the municipal assembly. If the assembly is unable to convene." The next sentence reads: "The Crisis Staff shall submit all decisions on issues within the competence of the municipal assembly to the municipal assembly as soon as the assembly is able to convene." My question with regard to this is the following: Does this make clear the fact that Crisis Staff hereby avails itself of the competences of the municipal assembly?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC
utterances.text: These competences were already provided for in a relevant law. The Crisis Staff cannot avail itself of these competences. These were already regulated by law, except that in the relevant law, they are referred to -- this is referred to as the National Defence Council. The body in question is the National Defence Council and not the Crisis Staff and that is the main difference.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would just like to hear you with respect of this. There are no other competences that this Crisis Staff availed itself of, except from the competence that already apply to the municipal assembly in this area?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC
utterances.text: I have to emphasise that the role of the National Defence Council, whose competences were taken over by the Crisis Staff, are different -- differ depending on peacetime and wartime. A different situation applies in wartime. Second, the competences of the National Defence Council, and in this case the Crisis Staff, are different from the competences of the assembly. So these two things are not completely identical.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This decision makes no mention of the National Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we agree that the National Defence Council was also a body of the assembly, at the level of the municipality?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC
utterances.text: National Defence Council, because of its composition, could not be referred to as a body of the municipal assembly, because when you say a body, or an organ, you usually refer to a body which is directly subordinated to the municipal assembly. National Defence Council is much more complex than that, in terms of its competences. If you want me to, I can provide you a brief explanation of these differences.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, gentlemen, stop, both of you, because I think we are beating around the bush. There is no way Article 3 can be read on its own, without reference to Article 2 that precedes it, which spells out actually in broad terms the terms of reference, the various terms of reference, of the Prijedor municipal Crisis Staff. Article 3 refers only to the function of the Prijedor municipal Crisis Staff, should the municipal assembly be unable to sit in session. But the real terms of reference and powers and functions of the municipal Crisis Staff of Prijedor are in Article 2 and not in Article 3 and there, inter alia you also have the function of coordinating the Defence of the municipal territory. And no one would have expected the municipal Crisis Staff to incorporate either in Article 2 or in any other article, the coordination of the defence of the national territory. So let's move forward to some other relevant question. Yes, Mr. Koumjian?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: If I can make a quick comment. I happen to know there is a further translation somewhere in the OTP. This stops at Article 4 and does not include, for example, Article 6 which deals with defence matters. But we'll bring that down and have that to the court today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's Exhibit -- what was Exhibit S110 in Stakic has from Article 1 right through Article 15, which seems to be the last article, and which is signed then eventually or -- by Dr. Milomir Stakic. So we have the entire document here. Thank you. Yes, Mr. Trbojevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just wanted to ask the witness for his opinion regarding the text of this decision, from which we can see what it says, what is written there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He has confirmed to you that basically it was the entity that counted in the circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the relationship between the municipal Crisis Staff and the Regional Crisis Staff? Specifically, I'm talking about Prijedor and the ARK in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC
utterances.text: I did have occasion to see certain documents in the previous case, in the Stakic case, in which the competences of the Crisis Staff of the region are more specifically defined in relation to municipal leaderships, and I think they were defined in one of the documents. I think it was the founding document of the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Bosanska Krajina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to know whether you know what the relationship was between the Crisis Staff of Prijedor municipality and the Regional Crisis Staff. Let me tell you straight away, I don't have it here to show it to you, but Their Honours have already seen it. On the 22nd of June, the Prijedor Crisis Staff took a decision in which it stated that it did not recognise the decisions of the Crisis Staff of the region made prior to the 22nd of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Koumjian?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, the testimony of this witness in Stakic - it's part of the transcript - is that at that time, he was either trying to reach Bihac or had reached Bihac. There is no information that he would have had access to those documents and would just call for speculation on his part to guess as to what the relationship was between those two bodies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In any case, it's being put to him. He may have obtained information subsequent to his departure to Bihac. But I think the -- I will allow the question. Sir, it's being suggested to you that on or around the 22nd of June, the Prijedor Crisis Staff took a decision tantamount to declaring that they will not recognise any decision reached by the ARK Crisis Staff prior to that date. Are you aware of this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I'm not aware of this. I hear of that decision and of that document for the first time now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And if I confirm to you that this is so, that such decision was taken indeed on the 22nd of June by the Prijedor Crisis Staff, what would that mean to you with reference or in relation to the relationship that existed between the ARK Crisis Staff and the Regional Crisis Staff -- and the municipal Crisis Staff, and the Prijedor Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To be able to give a specific answer, Your Honours, and Mr. President, if possible, could I see that document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Gustin? We can show it to the witness if it can be --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This same Official Gazette, the same Official Gazette.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: If counsel has an exhibit number -- we can't find it right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Any way, let's not lose time. I am --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm told it's 1265.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 1265? See if you can find 1265.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unfortunately, it is the Official Gazette that hasn't been translated in its entirety.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but we have had an English translation of that part of the gazette too. What you have just said is correct, Mr. Trbojevic, when it was first mentioned it had not yet been translated but we had it translated there and then and it was made availability. So the English translation is available. Yes, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I think it maybe was introduced as a DB document and not a P document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It could be.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I think I did it on cross-examination with a translation that we did ourselves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I think. That's my recollection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think you're correct, you are right, Mr. Ackerman. Any way, the position is this: That at a certain time on the 22nd of June, or there about, the Prijedor municipal council declared openly that it will not recognise the decisions of the ARK Crisis Staff taken before or up to that date. What would this mean that there was good blood or bad blood in the relationship existing between the ARK Crisis Staff and the Prijedor -- it's Crisis Staff, the Crisis Staff of Prijedor, and the ARK Crisis Staff? Were the relations, according to you, good or bad? Or could this decision be explained by reference to some other important matter? That you may be aware of. If you're not aware of it, or if you're not in a position to answer the question, please say so, and we move to the next question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, Your Honour, you asked me about the substantial relationships between the municipal staff and the Regional Crisis Staff. Judging by a number of documents that I saw in the Stakic case, and also judging by what I heard after I left Prijedor, those relationships were mostly good. What I'm saying is there was a certain hierarchical superiority of the regional staff and that -- and it functioned. Now, whether there were any misunderstandings and what the nature of those misunderstandings were, which could be gleaned from the document you are mentioning, but without seeing the document itself, you will realise it's difficult for me to make any kind of judgement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Next. We stop for one minute or two, until they change the tape and we continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Trbojevic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In view of the answer, I must ask you, which documents you saw, what kind of documents? What was the content of those documents or the gist of those documents, please, regarding this hierarchy between the municipality and the ARK?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC
utterances.text: All those documents are to be found in the evidence in the Stakic case, but I will now present the substance from some of those documents. For instance --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do we need to go through all this if they are in the Stakic records -- if they are exhibits in the Stakic records, which we all have here?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think that this particular point cannot be found in those documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So that's your point of view, and he differs from that. I mean, but the documents that he will obviously be referring to are the same documents which, according to you, would not lead to the same conclusion. So let's leave it at that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You're not going to change your positions in any case. The documents are what they are. They are not going to change either. So...

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have to ask you, but a moment ago, speaking about Mr. Brdjanin, you said that he advocated the position that citizens should be humanely resettled. I'm paraphrasing and simplifying, of course. Because in your most recent statement, you said that you had heard him say in the assembly that it would be a good idea if there would be only a few percent of non-Serbs in Serbian municipalities, et cetera, et cetera. I should now like to ask the witness to be shown Defence Exhibit 80, DB80. It's a short text and we'll go through it quickly. This is again a photocopy of an Official Gazette. I think the conclusions are at the bottom of the page under number 23. Can you see it? It's rather a poor copy. These are conclusions of the ARK dated the 29th of May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Trbojevic, is it DB80 or DB0126? Because what we are seeing on the monitor now is what you handed down to us today as DB0126.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we did have it marked today as 0126, but I was informed a moment ago that it had already been admitted into evidence as DB80.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So it's not being admitted into evidence today. It has already been admitted into evidence. Okay. Thank you. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you been able to read this text?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC
utterances.text: Yes. Part of the text in Cyrillic script are difficult to read, but thanks to the English translation, I have managed to read the whole text. Actually, this conclusion that you referred to -- you mean, right up until the end, the President of the Crisis Staff, Radoslav Brdjanin?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Can it be seen from this document that the Crisis Staff of the ARK, of the region, is here concluding, it is not ordering or determining or prescribing, but it allows for the need to have exchanges, family for family, at the request of those interested in such an exchange, on the basis of reciprocity. And in paragraph 3, the leaderships of the SDA and the HDZ are called upon to join in this process of humane resettlement. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC
utterances.text: If you wish to hear my comments regarding this conclusion, or do you need to confirm that what you have read is right? Yes, that is what it says.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, of course you may comment on it if you wish.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC
utterances.text: What is your question? I will answer your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is not a forum where comments are invited. You either put a question or you don't. And your question was whether it says what you read, and he said yes, it says exactly what you read. The suggestion was very clear that Mr. Brdjanin was advocating a peaceful resettlement of the population and not a radical one.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question is whether this is significantly different from what you described as Brdjanin's political view regarding resettlement.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC
utterances.text: What I said was that Mr. Brdjanin advocated resettlements, which can be clearly seen from this document. However, in this document, no mention is made of the highest percentage in these resettlements.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, please, you told us that according to Mr. Karadzic's criteria, Mr. Brdjanin was a good Serb, and you justified this with his relatively fast progress in terms of career. If I tell you that this Crisis Staff led by him lasted less than three months and that after that he was removed from the assembly as a deputy, would you still agree that a -- he had had a fast-moving career?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. What's your objection, Mr. Koumjian?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Well, I think the time he was removed from the assembly is very important. It's far beyond the indictment period. During the indictment period, he was moved to a minister position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's correct. Yes. Doctor, please, your answer to Mr. Trbojevic's question, keeping in mind that the removal of Mr. Brdjanin from the assembly was not immediately -- did not immediately follow the cessation of the existence of the ARK Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that the removal of Mr. Brdjanin from the assembly does not necessarily constitute a removal. His appointment to the position of the minister, according to the laws of Bosnia and Herzegovina, which to a significant extent also applied to the government of the then Republika Srpska, could not include at the same time, simultaneous offices of a member of parliament and minister. One single individual could not at the same time be a member of the executive and the legislative power, and that is why I think that Mr. Brdjanin was simply relieved of list duty as a member of parliament which was perfectly normal procedure and appointed to the position of the minister. In application of this principle that there should be no overlapping of the executive and the legislative power. So this mere fact cannot serve as a basis for the conclusion that Mr. Brdjanin, because of the fact that he had been relieved of his duty as a member of parliament, was demoted. I think if someone is appointed minister, it's actually a promotion, and it was a step higher up in his career.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You spoke about the information that could not be practically -- that is not correct. We cannot go into a debate about that at this point. I should like to focus on the events that took place in Hambarine on the 22nd of May. I think that you have provided four descriptions of the said event?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It was 35 minutes ago you told me you only --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have two more questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because we have to be fair to the interpreters and the technicians. If we said 15 to 20 minutes, we keep it to 15 and 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the transcript, on page 3.827, line 5, in the Stakic case, you said that the vehicle was shot at by a passer-by by the name of Habibovic who happened to have grabbed somebody else's rifle, opened fire, and who later perished in the Omarska camp. However, in the Tadic case, on page 55, line 84, you stated that it was a member of the TO that had opened fire on this vehicle, and that he shot with a burst of gunfire and targeted the vehicle and so on and so forth. So can you tell us now which version is accurate or more accurate?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC
utterances.text: Both versions are accurate. Not only one but several members of the -- actually, not the Territorial Defence, because the checkpoint was manned by the police. But if you're specifically referring to the person who actually shot at these -- at this vehicle, at these members, then it was Mr. Habibovic who fired.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that it was clear that the vehicle was carrying the extremist forces of SDS and that you could conclude that by the insignia, the signs, on the vehicle. What kind of insignia were those? Line 87 of the Tadic transcript.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC
utterances.text: I don't think I referred to the markings on the vehicle. I think I referred to the insignia on the uniforms of the soldiers who were in the vehicle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what kind of insignia those soldiers had on their uniforms? And how was it that they were visible when you said that they never left the car?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC
utterances.text: Well, they were eventually visible because a member of the checkpoint came close to the vehicle, approached the vehicle. He was probably 30 or 50 centimetres away from the vehicle. So surely he was able from that distance to see the insignia on the shoulders of these soldiers who were inside.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you very much. This concludes my examination, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Very quickly, two questions, I hope. Re-examined by Mr. Koumjian:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you mentioned in you are why earlier testimony a traditional rivalry between the Sarajevo SDS leadership and Banja Luka, that that was a traditional rivalry. Was there a similar traditional rivalry in the Krajina region between Prijedor and Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUJADZIC
utterances.text: Yes. I guess you could call it that way. There was a similar rivalry between Prijedor and Banja Luka. I think I mentioned it in the first portion of my testimony.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Secondly, you indicated -- you were shown a document in which the Crisis Staff is asking for resettlement of population. Given what you know about the Bosniak and Croat populations in the Krajina region in 1992, do you think it was possible to peacefully remove the great majority of those people from the homes that they were born in and lived in all their lives?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Trbojevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My learned friend is saying that the conclusions of the Crisis Staff of the region were asking for a resettlement. This was not the wording of the document. Conclusions imply that it is the wish or request of the people living there to exchange their places of residence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Any way, in any case, the witness's opinion isn't going to change anything, Mr. Koumjian. That decision will be taken -- or that consideration will be made by this Trial Chamber in its deliberations later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Sir, that brings us to an end. We have managed to finish your testimony today. And that enables you return to your place of residence, country of residence, as early as possible. I thank you for having accepted again, once more, to come to this Tribunal to give evidence in another trial. And you will be attended to by the officers of this Tribunal to assist you in your return. And I wish you a safe journey back home. Thank you. Tomorrow we continue with Colonel Selak. The exhibits?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Does Your Honour want me to go through them or perhaps --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think you can sort it out with the Registrar and -- provided you keep Mr. Ackerman or Mr. Trbojevic informed, it can be done. If there is a difficulty, then you will refer to us and we will decide accordingly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: We are moving all of the exhibits from the Stakic testimony into evidence. Many of them, most of them are already in evidence but I don't know if there is any objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If there is a problem, obviously when in doubt, don't refer it to us and we will decide. I thank you all and my apologies to the interpreters and the rest of the staff. I assure you it was all non-intentional and I'm sure we have your forgiveness and understanding. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 6.03 p.m., to be reconvened on Thursday, the 23rd day of January, 2003, at 2.15 p.m.
